items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1967-10-28
items.q: they and Jack Lane were the only two bands in town at that time that was doing that

ctx.x: Back in those days, did your father and the other people who were playing that kind of music think of themselves as jazz musicians, as doing something different?

Oh, yes, because they were the only band, they and Jack Lane were the only two bands in town at that time that was doing that, you see. And that's why the name, the Ragtime Military Jazz Band, because they'd play anything. They'd play parades. They'd play funerals, weddings, anything like that. And then they'd play these all-day picnics where they would play jazz. But the instrumentation in those days was much different, Doug, than it is now. There were no saxophones. In those days, a band usually consisted of…
Would it have sounded anything like, say, the Olympia or the Onward sound of the day?

items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: That's the only time I ever saw Jack play double drums... But he mostly, mostly his, his work mostly was parades, picnics, things like that.

ctx.x: Well, this Owls Hall, it was just about a block down from the ferry landing. And they would do, if they caught you fooling, the fellas over there would go up the fellas from New Orleans fooling with any of the girls. Well, they'd do either one of two things. They'd either run them up the levee and down the ferry landing. If the ferry wasn't in, don't stop, just keep going, you know. Either that or the two fellas would get the guy, one by the arms and one by the legs and take him by a window like that and swing…
You ever played any of his bands? No, I never did.
